summary: 2 blocking question(s) must be answered before design

questions.question: What are the measurable campaign targets: expected peak redirect requests per second or concurrent visitors, the redirect latency target (p95/p99), and the availability goal during the campaign window?
questions.why: The target decides the architecture. Modest load can be met with the WAL/pool/lean-query changes in this spec. Medium load requires a PostgreSQL deployment and driver. Large load needs caching and asynchronous click ingestion, which conflict with immediate deactivation and synchronous counts and cannot be delivered safely in one week.
options: Modest: up to about 50 RPS, p95 < 100 ms, best effort (one instance is enough)
Medium: about 500 RPS, p95 < 100 ms, 99.9% availability (needs PostgreSQL and several workers)
Large: several thousand RPS or TV-spike bursts (needs PostgreSQL, multiple replicas, possibly an edge cache and an asynchronous click pipeline)
questions.default: Modest-to-medium load on a single deployment. The CI acceptance bar is NFR-10 (16 concurrent clients, zero 5xx, p95 < 250 ms), and production sizing is documented as guidance, not guaranteed.

questions.question: Which database and topology will serve the campaign in production: SQLite on one instance, or PostgreSQL/MySQL with several workers or replicas? If PostgreSQL, should we pin a driver (e.g. psycopg) in requirements.txt?
questions.why: SQLite stays single-writer even with WAL, so the click write per visit limits throughput. If production is PostgreSQL or MySQL, we must add and pin a driver, validate the pool defaults for it, and FR-19's collation fix becomes urgent. A multi-instance topology also rules out any in-process cache.
options: PostgreSQL with several workers/replicas, and a pinned driver added
MySQL with several workers/replicas, and a pinned driver added
questions.default: Keep whatever backend is deployed today, add no driver, make SQLite as robust as possible (WAL, busy_timeout), make the pool configurable, and document that campaign-scale or multi-worker deployments should move to PostgreSQL.

payload.requirement:
Marketing is launching a big campaign next week and will put our short links on billboards and
in a TV ad. Make the link service faster and more trustworthy before then.

answers.Q-1: Modest: up to about 50 RPS, p95 < 100 ms, best effort (one instance is enough)
answers.Q-2: Keep the current SQLite backend and harden it (WAL, busy_timeout, configurable pool). Add no new driver. Document the move to PostgreSQL for multi-worker or campaign scale.

summary: Approve architecture & plan: 7 endpoints, 3 entities, 7 work packages, 8 ADRs

api_contract: POST /api/links — Create a short link (unchanged). Requires X-API-Key. Optional Idempotency-Key header.
GET /api/links/{code} — Link metadata with all-time total_clicks (unchanged). Requires X-API-Key.
DELETE /api/links/{code} — Soft-deactivate a link, idempotent (unchanged). Requires X-API-Key. The next GET or HEAD /{code} returns 410 immediately.
GET /api/links/{code}/stats — Click stats with SQL-side daily aggregation (bounded memory). Response schema and semantics unchanged. Requires X-API-Key.

GET /{code} — Public redirect, registered last. GET does a narrow lookup (one SELECT of id, url, is_active), then one INSERT into click_events and one COMMIT. If the click write fails or times out, it is rolled back, one WARNING is logged and the visitor still gets the 307. HEAD /{code} (unchanged handler, include_in_schema=False) gives the same statuses and headers with no click, one SELECT and no INSERT.

GET /healthz — Liveness probe; never touches the DB (unchanged). New: HEAD /healthz (a separate route, include_in_schema=False) returns 200 with an empty body, does no DB access and runs no link lookup. POST /healthz still returns 405.

GET /readyz — Readiness probe running SELECT 1 (unchanged). New: HEAD /readyz (a separate route, include_in_schema=False) runs the same SELECT 1 check, never a links lookup, and returns 200 with an empty body or 503 from the readiness check. POST /readyz still returns 405.

work_packages.title: Core: new settings, hardened engine factory, tuning description, log field
App factory wiring: tuned engine and startup tuning log
Documentation: README, API reference, runbook and changelog

decisions: ADR-1 Harden SQLite at the engine level: WAL and synchronous=NORMAL through a connect event, busy_timeout through the pysqlite timeout connect arg: For file-based SQLite URLs, create_db_engine registers a 'connect' event listener that calls apply_sqlite_pragmas(dbapi_connection). That function runs the literal statements 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL' and 'PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL' on a DBAPI cursor and tolerates failure: it logs a WARNING and continues in the existing journal mode. busy_timeout is set by passing connect_args={'check_same_thread': False, 'timeout': (SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS + 0.5) / 1000}. CPython computes sqlite3_busy_timeout as (int)(timeout*1000), so the +0.5 makes PRAGMA busy_timeout report exactly SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS with no float truncation. The default of 5000 equals today's pysqlite default.

ADR-2 Configurable pool only where a QueuePool exists: Pass pool_size, max_overflow and pool_timeout to create_engine for file-based SQLite (SQLAlchemy 2.0 uses QueuePool there) and for non-SQLite URLs. Do not pass them for in-memory SQLite ('sqlite://', ':memory:', 'mode=memory', 'file::memory:'), which uses SingletonThreadPool and would reject max_overflow and pool_timeout.

ADR-3 HEAD probes as dedicated hidden routes on the health router: Add @router.head('/healthz', include_in_schema=False) and @router.head('/readyz', include_in_schema=False), each returning an empty Response(200). The GET routes are unchanged. Readiness logic is shared through a private _check_ready(db) helper.

ADR-4 Stats daily buckets aggregated in SQL through a dialect-compiled UtcDate construct: click_repository defines class UtcDate(FunctionElement) with type=Date() and inherit_cache=True, compiled with sqlalchemy.ext.compiler.compiles. The default (PostgreSQL and others) compiles to CAST(x AS DATE); sqlite and mysql/mariadb compile to date(x) / DATE(x). The compiler functions delegate to compiler.process(cast(...)) and compiler.process(func.date(...)), so no SQL string formatting is needed. The query is GROUP BY day ORDER BY day for one link_id with created_at >= since. Referrer counts keep GROUP BY on the raw column; '' and NULL are merged in Python, and the service still sorts and caps at 10.

ADR-5 Narrow redirect lookup returning a NamedTuple, with no cache: LinkRepository.get_redirect_target(code) runs select(Link.id, Link.url, Link.is_active).where(Link.code == code) and returns RedirectTarget(id, url, is_active) or None. Redirect resolution uses it. Deactivation, detail and stats keep get_by_code. There is no redirect cache and no async click ingestion.

ADR-6 Click-failure logging at WARNING without exc_info: In resolve_and_record_click, any exception from the click add or commit is followed by session.rollback() (its own failure is suppressed) and exactly one logger.warning('failed to record click for link_id=%s error=%s', link_id, type(exc).__name__) on 'app.services.links'. There is no traceback and no exception message. The 307 is still returned.

ADR-7 MySQL case-sensitive codes through a portable type variant: Link.code = mapped_column(String(32).with_variant(String(32, collation='utf8mb4_bin'), 'mysql', 'mariadb'), nullable=False). The docs give the manual ALTER TABLE for existing MySQL databases.

ADR-8 Startup tuning log line built from the engine and settings, without the URL: core/db.py provides describe_db_tuning(engine, settings) -> dict and format_db_tuning(dict) -> str. In the lifespan after create_all, main.py logs on 'app.db' at INFO: message 'database tuning ' + format_db_tuning(tuning), with extra={'db_tuning': tuning}. 'db_tuning' is added to the JsonFormatter extra fields.

risks.description: WAL cannot be enabled (network filesystem, read-only directory) or behaves differently for in-memory URLs.
risks.mitigation: apply_sqlite_pragmas tolerates failure and logs a WARNING ('could not enable SQLite WAL journal mode'). In-memory URLs skip WAL entirely. The startup tuning log shows the effective journal_mode. OPERATIONS.md requires local writable disk. Unit test with a fake DBAPI connection whose cursor raises.

risks.description: Float truncation in pysqlite's timeout-to-milliseconds conversion makes PRAGMA busy_timeout differ by 1 ms from the setting.
risks.mitigation: sqlite_timeout_seconds(ms) returns (ms + 0.5) / 1000. A test asserts PRAGMA busy_timeout == the setting for 0, 200, 1000, 5000 and 60000.

risks.description: SQL day bucketing differs from the Python implementation (string dates on SQLite, edge-of-window comparison).
risks.mitigation: UtcDate has type=Date() so SQLite strings are parsed to date, and the repository also converts str with date.fromisoformat. The window filter is unchanged (created_at >= since). The existing tests/test_stats.py runs unmodified as the oracle. The three-dialect compile test covers the dialect guards.

risks.description: Under burst load, a click INSERT waits for the full busy_timeout (default 5 s), which raises redirect latency.
risks.mitigation: With WAL and synchronous=NORMAL, write transactions are sub-millisecond, so waits stay short. OPERATIONS.md recommends SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=1000 for the campaign. Each dropped click is logged once. NFR-19 tests the burst.

risks.description: Pool exhaustion: 16 or more concurrent requests exceed 5+10 connections and queue for up to 30 s.
risks.mitigation: Pool sizing is configurable. Campaign guidance is DB_POOL_SIZE=10, DB_MAX_OVERFLOW=10, DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=10, which stays at or below the 40 threadpool tokens. Requests release connections quickly.

risks.description: Swallowing all click-write exceptions could hide programming errors.
risks.mitigation: This is existing behaviour (best effort, by design). The WARNING line includes the exception class name, and OPERATIONS.md tells operators to alert on sustained 'failed to record click'.

risks.description: Implementers change public signatures used by tests: ClickRepository.add is monkeypatched in an existing test, and LinkService.get_link_detail is monkeypatched as well.
risks.mitigation: The work packages require keeping ClickRepository.add, count_for_link and referrer_counts, LinkRepository.get_by_code, and all LinkService and StatsService public method signatures. The GET click insert must go through ClickRepository.add.

risks.description: Docs drift from the code: setting names, log messages and recommended values.
risks.mitigation: The docs package depends on the code packages and uses the exact names and messages fixed in this design. A test checks that every Settings env name appears in README.md, and a doc test checks the section headings.

The changes are small and behaviour-preserving, at the engine, query and routing level. There is no cache, no async click ingestion, no new dependency and no schema change to existing tables (the only exception is a MySQL-only collation variant).

1. Hardened SQLite engine (FR-15/FR-16). This lives in app/core/db.py. File-based SQLite gets WAL and synchronous=NORMAL through a connect event, plus a busy_timeout taken from the new setting SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS (passed as pysqlite's `timeout` connect arg). A configurable QueuePool comes from DB_POOL_SIZE, DB_MAX_OVERFLOW and DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. In-memory SQLite ignores the pool settings and WAL. Non-SQLite URLs keep pool_pre_ping and get the pool settings. At startup, app.db logs one structured 'database tuning' line with no URL and no secrets (NFR-16).
2. Lean, contention-tolerant redirect path (FR-15/FR-17/NFR-12). LinkRepository.get_redirect_target runs SELECT id, url, is_active WHERE code=?. LinkService resolves through it. A click INSERT or COMMIT failure, such as a lock timeout, is rolled back and logged once at WARNING with no IP and no exception text. The visitor still gets the 307. A failed lookup still becomes a 503 JSON response through the existing SQLAlchemyError handler.
3. HEAD probes (FR-14). Separate HEAD /healthz and HEAD /readyz routes (include_in_schema=False) on the health router, which is registered before the catch-all. The OpenAPI document stays byte-identical.

summary: Approve architecture & plan: 9 endpoints, 3 entities, 7 work packages, 10 ADRs

api_contract: POST /api/links — Create a short link. Requires X-API-Key. Optional Idempotency-Key header and optional expires_at.
GET /api/links/{code} — Get link metadata, including deactivated and expired links. Requires X-API-Key.
PATCH /api/links/{code} — Set, change or clear the expiry of an existing link. Requires X-API-Key.
DELETE /api/links/{code} — Deactivate (soft-delete) a link. Idempotent. Requires X-API-Key. Unchanged.
GET /api/links/{code}/stats — Daily click stats. Contract unchanged; now aggregated in SQL. Requires X-API-Key.
GET /api/links/{code}/stats/hourly — Clicks per UTC hour for one link over [start, end), zero-filled. Requires X-API-Key.
GET /{code} — Public redirect. Records exactly one click on success (best-effort). The HEAD /{code} twin (not in the schema) returns the same status and headers and records no click.
GET /healthz — Liveness probe; never touches the DB. HEAD /healthz (not in the schema) returns 200 with an empty body. POST returns 405.
GET /readyz — Readiness probe (SELECT 1). HEAD /readyz (not in the schema) returns 200 with an empty body, or 503. POST returns 405.

decisions:
ADR-1 Harden SQLite with a connect listener, connect_args timeout and QueuePool settings: For file-based SQLite:
- create_engine(url, poolclass=QueuePool, pool_size, max_overflow, pool_timeout, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False, 'timeout': (SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS + 0.5) / 1000.0}).
- An event.listens_for(engine, 'connect') handler executes the literal statements 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL' and 'PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL' on a raw DBAPI cursor.
- The +0.5 ms makes pysqlite's int(timeout*1000) truncation land exactly on the configured value.

In-memory SQLite gets only check_same_thread=False. Non-SQLite gets pool_pre_ping=True plus the pool settings.

ADR-2 Idempotent startup ALTER instead of migration tooling: After create_all, the lifespan calls app.core.schema.ensure_links_expires_at(engine):
- It uses sqlalchemy.inspect on a fresh connection.
- If 'expires_at' is not among the links columns, it runs the dialect-guarded literal ALTER inside engine.begin().
- It logs 'added' or 'already_present'.
- On any exception it logs an ERROR and re-raises, so startup aborts.

ADR-3 Expiry evaluated in Python on the narrow lookup row, with an injectable clock: LinkRepository.get_redirect_target selects only id, url, is_active and expires_at. LinkService._check_redirectable(target) raises GoneError() if the link is inactive, then GoneError(LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL) if expires_at is not None and self._utcnow() >= expires_at. GET and HEAD both go through _resolve_target, which calls _check_redirectable. The clock is LinkService(now=callable|None); _utcnow() calls it, falling back to models.utcnow(), and normalises to naive UTC.

ADR-4 Backward-compatible idempotency hash: request_hash = sha256(url) when expires_at is None; otherwise sha256(url + '\n' + canonical UTC instant 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ'). The replay check runs before the future-instant check.

ADR-5 SQL aggregation with dialect-guarded bucket expressions that use no bound parameters: Daily and hourly stats use SELECT bucket, COUNT(id) ... WHERE link_id = :id AND created_at >= :start [AND created_at < :end] GROUP BY bucket.

Day bucket:
- sqlite: func.date(created_at)
- postgresql (and the fallback): cast(created_at, Date)
- mysql/mariadb: func.date(created_at)

Hour bucket:
- sqlite: func.strftime(literal_column("'%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00'"), created_at)
- postgresql (and the fallback): func.date_trunc(literal_column("'hour'"), created_at)
- mysql/mariadb: func.timestampadd(literal_column('HOUR'), func.hour(created_at), func.date(created_at))

Result values are normalised in Python (str -> date/datetime). Module-level statement builders take dialect_name so tests can compile them for all three dialects.

ADR-6 Explicit HEAD routes for the probes: health.py adds @router.head('/healthz', include_in_schema=False) and @router.head('/readyz', include_in_schema=False). They return Response(status_code=200) with an empty body. /readyz shares a private _check_database(db) helper with GET.

ADR-7 End the read transaction before the click insert; best-effort WARNING on failure: In resolve_and_record_click, after the lookup and checks, call self.session.rollback(). This ends the read transaction and is a transaction-boundary call, not a statement. Then call ClickRepository.add(...) and session.commit() inside try/except Exception. On failure:
- Roll back, suppressing any secondary exception.
- Log exactly one logger.warning('failed to record click for link_id=%s (%s)', link_id, type(exc).__name__), with no IP, no exception message and no traceback.
- Return the URL.

ADR-8 Future-instant validation in the service with a 422 domain error: Add InvalidInputError(AppError) with status 422 in app/core/errors.py. Schemas only parse and normalise (to naive UTC, non-string values rejected). LinkService raises InvalidInputError('expires_at must be in the future') using its injectable clock. StatsService raises InvalidInputError for invalid hourly ranges.

ADR-9 No-store on redirect-path error responses: redirect.py catches NotFoundError and GoneError from the service and returns JSONResponse({'detail': exc.detail}, status_code=exc.status_code, headers={'Cache-Control': 'no-store'}). Other exceptions propagate to the global handlers (SQLAlchemyError -> 503).

ADR-10 MySQL case-sensitive codes via a type variant: Declare code as String(32).with_variant(String(32, collation='utf8mb4_bin'), 'mysql', 'mariadb'). Document the manual DDL for existing MySQL databases: ALTER TABLE links MODIFY code VARCHAR(32) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL;

risks.description: The startup upgrade is not applied or is wrong, so every links query fails on the production DB (503 on every redirect).
risks.mitigation: Idempotent ensure_links_expires_at in the lifespan, which fails startup on error. Test against an old-schema SQLite file with existing rows and idempotency keys. Back up before deploying (runbook). Document the manual SQL.

risks.description: Pool kwargs passed for in-memory SQLite raise at create_app('sqlite://').
risks.mitigation: The in-memory branch passes only check_same_thread. Tests cover 'sqlite://' and ':memory:'.

risks.description: SQL bucketing differs from the old Python bucketing (window edges, ordering, return types).
risks.mitigation: Keep the >= since predicate and sort in Python. Normalise str to date/datetime. The unmodified tests/test_stats.py is the oracle, plus hourly boundary tests and compile tests for three dialects.

risks.description: A naive vs aware comparison, or datetime overflow (year 9999 with an offset, +1 hour at datetime.max), raises a 500.
risks.mitigation: Everything is normalised to naive UTC at the schema and service boundaries. OverflowError is converted to ValueError (schemas) or InvalidInputError (services). Tests use +01:00, -05:00 and +05:30 and extreme values.

risks.description: '+' in hourly query strings decodes as a space, so the offset is misread and the request returns 422.
risks.mitigation: Document URL-encoding (%2B) or using 'Z' in API.md and the runbook. A parse failure is a clean 422, never a wrong answer.

risks.description: Click drops under bursts because of the short busy timeout recommended for the campaign.
risks.mitigation: Every drop logs one WARNING (countable per hour). Default 5000 ms, runbook value 1000 ms. NFR-19 burst test.

risks.mitigation: Runbook PATCH loop over the code list, verified with GET detail (expires_at, is_expired), as a pre-launch checklist item. PATCH allows correction.

risks.mitigation: OPERATIONS.md: use sqlite3 .backup or copy all three files while the service is stopped; local writable directory only. The startup line shows the effective journal_mode.

risks.mitigation: Strict per-file ownership. Interfaces (names and signatures) are fixed in this design.

impl_report:WP-1.summary:
I implemented WP-1, the foundation package. Compile and ruff checks pass, and the existing tests pass. The test suite and app/main.py were not changed, so nothing new is covered by tests yet. The new engine branches, the startup schema upgrade and the engine tuning log line have not been run by any test or by the app.

What changed:
- **Settings:** four new validated settings: `SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` (0–60000, default 5000), `DB_POOL_SIZE` (≥1, default 5), `DB_MAX_OVERFLOW` (≥0, default 10) and `DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (>0 and ≤300, default 30). Existing settings are unchanged.
- **Database engine:** in-memory SQLite gets only `check_same_thread=False`. File-based SQLite gets a sized connection pool, the busy timeout through the sqlite3 `timeout` argument, and a connect listener that turns on WAL and `synchronous=NORMAL` using fixed strings. Other databases get `pool_pre_ping` plus the pool settings. New helpers `describe_engine` and `log_engine_tuning` report the effective settings without the URL.
- **Schema upgrade:** new `app/core/schema.py` with `ensure_links_expires_at(engine)`. It adds `links.expires_at` only if the column is missing (using the PostgreSQL column type on PostgreSQL), logs either "added" or "already present", and on failure logs an error and re-raises so startup aborts.
- **Errors and logging:** added `InvalidInputError` (422) and `LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL = 'Link has expired'`. The JSON log formatter now includes the tuning and schema-upgrade fields.
- **Models:** new `to_naive_utc()` helper, exported from `app.models`. `Link` gains a nullable `expires_at` column. `links.code` uses the case-sensitive `utf8mb4_bin` collation on MySQL/MariaDB only, without dialect-specific imports.
notes: Checks run: `python -m compileall -q app` and `ruff check app/core app/models` pass, and `python -m pytest -q` (existing suite) is green.
All SQL in core is fixed literal strings. The only formatted string is the tuning log message, which is not SQL. Core does not import app.api, app.services or app.repositories.
`create_engine` is called through the module-level name in `app.core.db`, so tests can monkeypatch it.

impl_report:WP-4.summary:
I implemented WP-4 in the two service files. All 165 existing tests pass, `python -m compileall -q app` succeeds and `ruff check app tests` is clean. No new tests were written; those belong to the test agent.

**`app/services/link_service.py`**
- **Clock and expiry:** `LinkService` takes an optional `now` clock. `_utcnow()` uses it and otherwise falls back to the module-level `utcnow`, looked up at call time so monkeypatching still works, and returns naive UTC. A link is expired when now ≥ `expires_at`.
- **Redirects:** GET and HEAD both go through the same `_resolve_target` helper. Malformed codes return 404 without any SQL; otherwise the helper does one narrow `get_redirect_target` SELECT and calls `_check_redirectable`. That check returns 410 for a deactivated link first, then 410 `Link has expired`.
- **Click recording:** `resolve_and_record_click` calls `session.rollback()` to end the read transaction before the click insert. A failed insert or commit is rolled back, any second rollback failure is suppressed, and exactly one WARNING is logged: `failed to record click for link_id=%s (%s)` with the exception class name only (no IP, message or traceback). The redirect still returns the URL.
- **`create_link`** has a new `expires_at` parameter. It is normalised to naive UTC, the idempotency replay/conflict check runs before the must-be-in-the-future check, and the new link is stored with `expires_at`.
- **Idempotency hash:** `_request_hash` is `sha256(url)` when there is no expiry, so keys stored before the deploy still replay. With an expiry it is `sha256(url + '\n' + '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ')`.
- **Detail and PATCH:** `LinkDetail` has a new `is_expired` field, which `get_link_detail` fills in. The new `set_expiry` looks the link up first (404), validates the value is in the future (422), commits only the `expires_at` change and returns the refreshed detail.
- **`deactivate`** now uses the injected clock.

**`app/services/stats_service.py`**
- `get_stats` keeps its signature and behaviour but now reads daily counts from `ClickRepository.daily_counts` (SQL `GROUP BY`) instead of counting in Python. The `Counter` import is gone.
- New `HourlyStats`, `MAX_HOURLY_RANGE_HOURS = 744` and `DEFAULT_HOURLY_LOOKBACK_HOURS = 24`.
- New `get_hourly_clicks` follows the WP steps (a) to (h) in order: both-or-neither check, UTC normalisation with OverflowError mapped to 422, default 25-hour window, start floored and end rounded up to the hour, start < end check, 744-hour cap, then the 404 check (works for deactivated and expired links), then zero-filled buckets and the total.
notes: I added two small private helpers not named in the WP: `LinkService._require_future`, shared by create and PATCH, and `StatsService._get_link_or_404`, shared by daily and hourly stats.
The best-effort rollback uses `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` instead of `try/except: pass`, because ruff rule S110 flags the latter. It behaves the same.
Error texts: 'expires_at must be in the future', 'start and end must be supplied together', 'datetime out of range', 'start must be before end' and 'range must not exceed 744 hours'.
The services import nothing from fastapi, starlette or app.api.

defects_found.description: Hourly stats put clicks in the wrong UTC hour on SQLite when the timestamp is within the last half-millisecond of an hour (FR-25, NFR-22). hour_bucket_expression('sqlite') uses strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', created_at), and SQLite rounds fractional seconds to milliseconds. A click stored at 2025-12-31 23:59:59.999999 (or anything from .9995) is bucketed as '2026-01-01 23:00:00': the date rolls over but the hour stays 23, so the click lands 24 hours late. It is then missing from the requested range and from total_clicks (the expected 23:00Z count is 2, the actual is 1). In other hours such clicks move into the next hour. Clicks are stored with microsecond precision from utcnow(), so this happens in production, roughly one click in 7,200. Daily stats are not affected (tested). A possible fix is to strip fractional seconds before bucketing (for example strftime over substr(created_at, 1, 19)) or to bucket in Python.

In-memory SQLite URLs cannot serve link requests (FR-15 / FR-16). FR-15 requires that for 'sqlite://' and ':memory:' the app 'starts and serves requests without error'. The app starts and /healthz and /readyz return 200, but POST /api/links returns 503 because of 'sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: links'. create_db_engine passes only check_same_thread=False for in-memory URLs, so SQLAlchemy uses SingletonThreadPool. That gives each thread its own in-memory database: the tables created by create_all on the lifespan thread are invisible to the request worker threads. This behaviour predates this change, but the new acceptance criterion requires it to work. Likely fix: use poolclass=StaticPool for in-memory SQLite (still without QueuePool kwargs).

repair_report_1.summary:
Fixed the two root causes behind the 3 failing tests. The full suite now passes: 404 passed, 0 failed, and ruff is clean.

(1) In-memory SQLite returned 503 'no such table: links'. For 'sqlite://' and ':memory:', SQLAlchemy's default SingletonThreadPool gives every thread its own connection, and each connection is a separate empty in-memory database. The tables created at startup were therefore invisible to requests running in FastAPI's worker threads. create_db_engine now uses poolclass=StaticPool (with check_same_thread=False) for in-memory SQLite, so all threads share one connection and one database. Pool sizing is still ignored there, there is no WAL and the pool is not a QueuePool, as FR-15/FR-16 require.

(2) Hourly (and daily) SQL bucketing was wrong for timestamps with sub-millisecond precision. SQLite's date functions round fractional seconds, and the installed SQLite 3.45.1 even maps '2025-12-31 23:59:59.999999' to 2026-01-01; I confirmed this with a probe. The click therefore fell outside the requested range and the 23:00 bucket showed 1 instead of 2. The SQLite day and hour bucket expressions now cut the stored text to whole seconds first: date(substr(created_at, 1, 19)) and strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', substr(created_at, 1, 19)). The positions are literal_column, so the bucket expressions still carry no bound parameters. The WHERE range predicates are unchanged, so the (link_id, created_at) index is still used (EXPLAIN test passes). PostgreSQL and MySQL expressions are unchanged.

# Release v1.2.0 — Campaign readiness: hardened single-instance SQLite redirects (50 RPS / p95 < 100 ms), automatic link expiry at campaign end, hourly click analytics, trustworthy probes, and accurate docs

Next week marketing starts a billboard and TV campaign that will show our short links to the public. The product owner has set the targets (Q-1): peak load is modest, up to about 50 redirect requests per second. Redirect p95 latency must be under 100 ms. Availability is best effort on one instance. Production stays on SQLite, hardened with WAL, a busy_timeout and a configurable pool (Q-2). No new database driver is added. The move to PostgreSQL for multi-worker or larger scale is documented but not implemented.

Amendment amd_5305a8421c78 adds two product needs:
(a) Campaign links must stop working on their own when the campaign ends (31 December, 23:59 UTC), with no one deactivating links by hand.
(b) Marketing must be able to see how many clicks each link got in each hour during the TV ad slots.

The current service has these defects or gaps for campaign traffic:
(1) SQLite has no hardening: no WAL, the default busy timeout and no pool configuration. Redirect lookups block behind click and create commits, and the runbook describes this behaviour wrongly.
(2) Pool sizing cannot be configured.
(3) HEAD /healthz and HEAD /readyz fall through to the catch-all HEAD /{code} route and return 404, so HEAD-based uptime monitors would report an outage.
(4) Stats load one row per click, so memory and time grow without limit.
(5) Links cannot expire. Redirect resolution checks only is_active.
(6) Analytics are bucketed only by UTC day, so clicks during an ad slot cannot be measured.
(7) There is no migration tooling. create_all never alters existing tables, so adding a column without an upgrade step would make every redirect against the production database return 503.
(8) On MySQL, codes match case-insensitively. This is low priority because production is SQLite.
(9) The docs contradict the code on authentication.

This change does the following:
- Makes the redirect path fast and resistant to contention on one SQLite instance.
- Makes DB tuning configurable.
- Adds a per-link expires_at that is enforced on GET and HEAD, can be set at creation or on existing links, and is applied to deployed databases by an idempotent startup schema upgrade.
- Adds a bounded, API-key-protected hourly click endpoint.
- Makes the probes and analytics trustworthy.
- Corrects the docs and adds a campaign runbook.

Every existing contract must stay intact: a 307 with the exact Location header and no-store; an immediate 410 after deactivation; synchronous click counting; privacy; the unchanged daily stats contract; idempotency replays of keys stored before the deploy; and the architecture rules. The deadline is one week, so the scope favours small, low-risk changes. That means no caching, no asynchronous ingestion, no new drivers, and only one additive, nullable schema change. New ids continue from FR-1..FR-21 and NFR-1..NFR-20.

## Delivered requirements
- **FR-14** HEAD support on liveness and readiness probes — verified by tests
- **FR-15** Redirects resilient to database write contention (hardened SQLite) — verified by tests
- **FR-16** Configurable database connection pool — verified by tests
- **FR-17** Lean redirect query budget — not traced
- **FR-18** Bounded-memory daily stats aggregation — verified by tests
- **FR-19** Case-sensitive short-code matching on MySQL — not traced
- **FR-20** Accurate documentation, campaign runbook and changelog — verified by tests
- **FR-21** Regression protection of existing contracts — verified by tests
- **FR-22** Automatic link expiry enforced on redirect — verified by tests
- **FR-23** Set expiry on link creation and expose it in responses — verified by tests
- **FR-24** Set, change or clear expiry on existing links — verified by tests
- **FR-25** Hourly click counts per link — verified by tests
- **FR-26** Idempotent startup schema upgrade for links.expires_at — verified by tests

## API
- `POST /api/links` — Create a short link. Requires X-API-Key. Optional Idempotency-Key header and optional expires_at.
- `GET /api/links/{code}` — Get link metadata, including deactivated and expired links. Requires X-API-Key.
- `PATCH /api/links/{code}` — Set, change or clear the expiry of an existing link. Requires X-API-Key.
- `DELETE /api/links/{code}` — Deactivate (soft-delete) a link. Idempotent. Requires X-API-Key. Unchanged.
- `GET /api/links/{code}/stats` — Daily click stats. Contract unchanged; now aggregated in SQL. Requires X-API-Key.
- `GET /api/links/{code}/stats/hourly` — Clicks per UTC hour for one link over [start, end), zero-filled. Requires X-API-Key.
- `GET /{code}` — Public redirect. Records exactly one click on success (best-effort). The HEAD /{code} twin (not in the schema) returns the same status and headers and records no click.
- `GET /healthz` — Liveness probe; never touches the DB. HEAD /healthz (not in the schema) returns 200 with an empty body. POST returns 405.
- `GET /readyz` — Readiness probe (SELECT 1). HEAD /readyz (not in the schema) returns 200 with an empty body, or 503. POST returns 405.

## Quality
- Tests: 404 passed, 0 failed
- Coverage: 99.78%
- Security findings: 6 (0 high/critical)

## Architecture decisions
- ADR-1 Harden SQLite with a connect listener, connect_args timeout and QueuePool settings: For file-based SQLite:
- create_engine(url, poolclass=QueuePool, pool_size, max_overflow, pool_timeout, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False, 'timeout': (SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS + 0.5) / 1000.0}).
- An event.listens_for(engine, 'connect') handler executes the literal statements 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL' and 'PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL' on a raw DBAPI cursor.
- The +0.5 ms makes pysqlite's int(timeout*1000) truncation land exactly on the configured value.

In-memory SQLite gets only check_same_thread=False. Non-SQLite gets pool_pre_ping=True plus the pool settings.
- ADR-2 Idempotent startup ALTER instead of migration tooling: After create_all, the lifespan calls app.core.schema.ensure_links_expires_at(engine):
- It uses sqlalchemy.inspect on a fresh connection.
- If 'expires_at' is not among the links columns, it runs the dialect-guarded literal ALTER inside engine.begin().
- It logs 'added' or 'already_present'.
- On any exception it logs an ERROR and re-raises, so startup aborts.
- ADR-3 Expiry evaluated in Python on the narrow lookup row, with an injectable clock: LinkRepository.get_redirect_target selects only id, url, is_active and expires_at. LinkService._check_redirectable(target) raises GoneError() if the link is inactive, then GoneError(LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL) if expires_at is not None and self._utcnow() >= expires_at. GET and HEAD both go through _resolve_target, which calls _check_redirectable. The clock is LinkService(now=callable|None); _utcnow() calls it, falling back to models.utcnow(), and normalises to naive UTC.
- ADR-4 Backward-compatible idempotency hash: request_hash = sha256(url) when expires_at is None; otherwise sha256(url + '\n' + canonical UTC instant 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ'). The replay check runs before the future-instant check.
- ADR-5 SQL aggregation with dialect-guarded bucket expressions that use no bound parameters: Daily and hourly stats use SELECT bucket, COUNT(id) ... WHERE link_id = :id AND created_at >= :start [AND created_at < :end] GROUP BY bucket.

Day bucket:
- sqlite: func.date(created_at)
- postgresql (and the fallback): cast(created_at, Date)
- mysql/mariadb: func.date(created_at)

Hour bucket:
- sqlite: func.strftime(literal_column("'%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00'"), created_at)
- postgresql (and the fallback): func.date_trunc(literal_column("'hour'"), created_at)
- mysql/mariadb: func.timestampadd(literal_column('HOUR'), func.hour(created_at), func.date(created_at))

Result values are normalised in Python (str -> date/datetime). Module-level statement builders take dialect_name so tests can compile them for all three dialects.
- ADR-6 Explicit HEAD routes for the probes: health.py adds @router.head('/healthz', include_in_schema=False) and @router.head('/readyz', include_in_schema=False). They return Response(status_code=200) with an empty body. /readyz shares a private _check_database(db) helper with GET.
- ADR-7 End the read transaction before the click insert; best-effort WARNING on failure: In resolve_and_record_click, after the lookup and checks, call self.session.rollback(). This ends the read transaction and is a transaction-boundary call, not a statement. Then call ClickRepository.add(...) and session.commit() inside try/except Exception. On failure:
- Roll back, suppressing any secondary exception.
- Log exactly one logger.warning('failed to record click for link_id=%s (%s)', link_id, type(exc).__name__), with no IP, no exception message and no traceback.
- Return the URL.
- ADR-8 Future-instant validation in the service with a 422 domain error: Add InvalidInputError(AppError) with status 422 in app/core/errors.py. Schemas only parse and normalise (to naive UTC, non-string values rejected). LinkService raises InvalidInputError('expires_at must be in the future') using its injectable clock. StatsService raises InvalidInputError for invalid hourly ranges.
- ADR-9 No-store on redirect-path error responses: redirect.py catches NotFoundError and GoneError from the service and returns JSONResponse({'detail': exc.detail}, status_code=exc.status_code, headers={'Cache-Control': 'no-store'}). Other exceptions propagate to the global handlers (SQLAlchemyError -> 503).
- ADR-10 MySQL case-sensitive codes via a type variant: Declare code as String(32).with_variant(String(32, collation='utf8mb4_bin'), 'mysql', 'mariadb'). Document the manual DDL for existing MySQL databases: ALTER TABLE links MODIFY code VARCHAR(32) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL;

## Known risks
- The startup upgrade is not applied or is wrong, so every links query fails on the production DB (503 on every redirect). — mitigation: Idempotent ensure_links_expires_at in the lifespan, which fails startup on error. Test against an old-schema SQLite file with existing rows and idempotency keys. Back up before deploying (runbook). Document the manual SQL.
- Pool kwargs passed for in-memory SQLite raise at create_app('sqlite://'). — mitigation: The in-memory branch passes only check_same_thread. Tests cover 'sqlite://' and ':memory:'.
- SQL bucketing differs from the old Python bucketing (window edges, ordering, return types). — mitigation: Keep the >= since predicate and sort in Python. Normalise str to date/datetime. The unmodified tests/test_stats.py is the oracle, plus hourly boundary tests and compile tests for three dialects.
- A naive vs aware comparison, or datetime overflow (year 9999 with an offset, +1 hour at datetime.max), raises a 500. — mitigation: Everything is normalised to naive UTC at the schema and service boundaries. OverflowError is converted to ValueError (schemas) or InvalidInputError (services). Tests use +01:00, -05:00 and +05:30 and extreme values.
- '+' in hourly query strings decodes as a space, so the offset is misread and the request returns 422. — mitigation: Document URL-encoding (%2B) or using 'Z' in API.md and the runbook. A parse failure is a clean 422, never a wrong answer.
- Click drops under bursts because of the short busy timeout recommended for the campaign. — mitigation: Every drop logs one WARNING (countable per hour). Default 5000 ms, runbook value 1000 ms. NFR-19 burst test.
- Operators enter the wrong expiry instant or year, or miss campaign links. — mitigation: Runbook PATCH loop over the code list, verified with GET detail (expires_at, is_expired), as a pre-launch checklist item. PATCH allows correction.
- The WAL sidecar files break naive backups or network filesystems. — mitigation: OPERATIONS.md: use sqlite3 .backup or copy all three files while the service is stopped; local writable directory only. The startup line shows the effective journal_mode.
- Overlapping concurrent work packages edit shared files. — mitigation: Strict per-file ownership. Interfaces (names and signatures) are fixed in this design.

(8) On MySQL, codes match case-insensitively. This is low priority because production is SQLite.
(9) The docs contradict the code on authentication.

This change does the following:
- Makes the redirect path fast and resistant to contention on one SQLite instance.
- Makes DB tuning configurable.
- Adds a per-link expires_at that is enforced on GET and HEAD, can be set at creation or on existing links, and is applied to deployed databases by an idempotent startup schema upgrade.
- Adds a bounded, API-key-protected hourly click endpoint.
- Makes the probes and analytics trustworthy.
- Corrects the docs and adds a campaign runbook.

Every existing contract must stay intact: a 307 with the exact Location header and no-store; an immediate 410 after deactivation; synchronous click counting; privacy; the unchanged daily stats contract; idempotency replays of keys stored before the deploy; and the architecture rules. The deadline is one week, so the scope favours small, low-risk changes. That means no caching, no asynchronous ingestion, no new drivers, and only one additive, nullable schema change. New ids continue from FR-1..FR-21 and NFR-1..NFR-20.

## Delivered requirements
- **FR-14** HEAD support on liveness and readiness probes — verified by tests
- **FR-15** Redirects resilient to database write contention (hardened SQLite) — verified by tests
- **FR-16** Configurable database connection pool — verified by tests
- **FR-17** Lean redirect query budget — not traced
- **FR-18** Bounded-memory daily stats aggregation — verified by tests
- **FR-19** Case-sensitive short-code matching on MySQL — not traced
- **FR-20** Accurate documentation, campaign runbook and changelog — verified by tests
- **FR-21** Regression protection of existing contracts — verified by tests
- **FR-22** Automatic link expiry enforced on redirect — verified by tests
- **FR-23** Set expiry on link creation and expose it in responses — verified by tests
- **FR-24** Set, change or clear expiry on existing links — verified by tests
- **FR-25** Hourly click counts per link — verified by tests
- **FR-26** Idempotent startup schema upgrade for links.expires_at — verified by tests

## API
- `POST /api/links` — Create a short link. Requires X-API-Key. Optional Idempotency-Key header and optional expires_at.
- `GET /api/links/{code}` — Get link metadata, including deactivated and expired links. Requires X-API-Key.
- `PATCH /api/links/{code}` — Set, change or clear the expiry of an existing link. Requires X-API-Key.
- `DELETE /api/links/{code}` — Deactivate (soft-delete) a link. Idempotent. Requires X-API-Key. Unchanged.
- `GET /api/links/{code}/stats` — Daily click stats. Contract unchanged; now aggregated in SQL. Requires X-API-Key.
- `GET /api/links/{code}/stats/hourly` — Clicks per UTC hour for one link over [start, end), zero-filled. Requires X-API-Key.
- `GET /{code}` — Public redirect. Records exactly one click on success (best-effort). The HEAD /{code} twin (not in the schema) returns the same status and headers and records no click.
- `GET /healthz` — Liveness probe; never touches the DB. HEAD /healthz (not in the schema) returns 200 with an empty body. POST returns 405.
- `GET /readyz` — Readiness probe (SELECT 1). HEAD /readyz (not in the schema) returns 200 with an empty body, or 503. POST returns 405.

## Quality
- Tests: 404 passed, 0 failed
- Coverage: 99.78%
- Security findings: 6 (0 high/critical)

## Architecture decisions
- ADR-1 Harden SQLite with a connect listener, connect_args timeout and QueuePool settings: For file-based SQLite:
- create_engine(url, poolclass=QueuePool, pool_size, max_overflow, pool_timeout, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False, 'timeout': (SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS + 0.5) / 1000.0}).
- An event.listens_for(engine, 'connect') handler executes the literal statements 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL' and 'PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL' on a raw DBAPI cursor.
- The +0.5 ms makes pysqlite's int(timeout*1000) truncation land exactly on the configured value.

In-memory SQLite gets only check_same_thread=False. Non-SQLite gets pool_pre_ping=True plus the pool settings.
- ADR-2 Idempotent startup ALTER instead of migration tooling: After create_all, the lifespan calls app.core.schema.ensure_links_expires_at(engine):
- It uses sqlalchemy.inspect on a fresh connection.
- If 'expires_at' is not among the links columns, it runs the dialect-guarded literal ALTER inside engine.begin().
- It logs 'added' or 'already_present'.
- On any exception it logs an ERROR and re-raises, so startup aborts.
- ADR-3 Expiry evaluated in Python on the narrow lookup row, with an injectable clock: LinkRepository.get_redirect_target selects only id, url, is_active and expires_at. LinkService._check_redirectable(target) raises GoneError() if the link is inactive, then GoneError(LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL) if expires_at is not None and self._utcnow() >= expires_at. GET and HEAD both go through _resolve_target, which calls _check_redirectable. The clock is LinkService(now=callable|None); _utcnow() calls it, falling back to models.utcnow(), and normalises to naive UTC.
- ADR-4 Backward-compatible idempotency hash: request_hash = sha256(url) when expires_at is None; otherwise sha256(url + '\n' + canonical UTC instant 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ'). The replay check runs before the future-instant check.
- ADR-5 SQL aggregation with dialect-guarded bucket expressions that use no bound parameters: Daily and hourly stats use SELECT bucket, COUNT(id) ... WHERE link_id = :id AND created_at >= :start [AND created_at < :end] GROUP BY bucket.

Day bucket:
- sqlite: func.date(created_at)
- postgresql (and the fallback): cast(created_at, Date)
- mysql/mariadb: func.date(created_at)

Hour bucket:
- sqlite: func.strftime(literal_column("'%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00'"), created_at)
- postgresql (and the fallback): func.date_trunc(literal_column("'hour'"), created_at)
- mysql/mariadb: func.timestampadd(literal_column('HOUR'), func.hour(created_at), func.date(created_at))

Result values are normalised in Python (str -> date/datetime). Module-level statement builders take dialect_name so tests can compile them for all three dialects.
- ADR-6 Explicit HEAD routes for the probes: health.py adds @router.head('/healthz', include_in_schema=False) and @router.head('/readyz', include_in_schema=False). They return Response(status_code=200) with an empty body. /readyz shares a private _check_database(db) helper with GET.
- ADR-7 End the read transaction before the click insert; best-effort WARNING on failure: In resolve_and_record_click, after the lookup and checks, call self.session.rollback(). This ends the read transaction and is a transaction-boundary call, not a statement. Then call ClickRepository.add(...) and session.commit() inside try/except Exception. On failure:
- Roll back, suppressing any secondary exception.
- Log exactly one logger.warning('failed to record click for link_id=%s (%s)', link_id, type(exc).__name__), with no IP, no exception message and no traceback.
- Return the URL.
- ADR-8 Future-instant validation in the service with a 422 domain error: Add InvalidInputError(AppError) with status 422 in app/core/errors.py. Schemas only parse and normalise (to naive UTC, non-string values rejected). LinkService raises InvalidInputError('expires_at must be in the future') using its injectable clock. StatsService raises InvalidInputError for invalid hourly ranges.
- ADR-9 No-store on redirect-path error responses: redirect.py catches NotFoundError and GoneError from the service and returns JSONResponse({'detail': exc.detail}, status_code=exc.status_code, headers={'Cache-Control': 'no-store'}). Other exceptions propagate to the global handlers (SQLAlchemyError -> 503).
- ADR-10 MySQL case-sensitive codes via a type variant: Declare code as String(32).with_variant(String(32, collation='utf8mb4_bin'), 'mysql', 'mariadb'). Document the manual DDL for existing MySQL databases: ALTER TABLE links MODIFY code VARCHAR(32) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL;

## Known risks
- The startup upgrade is not applied or is wrong, so every links query fails on the production DB (503 on every redirect). — mitigation: Idempotent ensure_links_expires_at in the lifespan, which fails startup on error. Test against an old-schema SQLite file with existing rows and idempotency keys. Back up before deploying (runbook). Document the manual SQL.
- Pool kwargs passed for in-memory SQLite raise at create_app('sqlite://'). — mitigation: The in-memory branch passes only check_same_thread. Tests cover 'sqlite://' and ':memory:'.
- SQL bucketing differs from the old Python bucketing (window edges, ordering, return types). — mitigation: Keep the >= since predicate and sort in Python. Normalise str to date/datetime. The unmodified tests/test_stats.py is the oracle, plus hourly boundary tests and compile tests for three dialects.
- A naive vs aware comparison, or datetime overflow (year 9999 with an offset, +1 hour at datetime.max), raises a 500. — mitigation: Everything is normalised to naive UTC at the schema and service boundaries. OverflowError is converted to ValueError (schemas) or InvalidInputError (services). Tests use +01:00, -05:00 and +05:30 and extreme values.
- '+' in hourly query strings decodes as a space, so the offset is misread and the request returns 422. — mitigation: Document URL-encoding (%2B) or using 'Z' in API.md and the runbook. A parse failure is a clean 422, never a wrong answer.
- Click drops under bursts because of the short busy timeout recommended for the campaign. — mitigation: Every drop logs one WARNING (countable per hour). Default 5000 ms, runbook value 1000 ms. NFR-19 burst test.
- Operators enter the wrong expiry instant or year, or miss campaign links. — mitigation: Runbook PATCH loop over the code list, verified with GET detail (expires_at, is_expired), as a pre-launch checklist item. PATCH allows correction.
- The WAL sidecar files break naive backups or network filesystems. — mitigation: OPERATIONS.md: use sqlite3 .backup or copy all three files while the service is stopped; local writable directory only. The startup line shows the effective journal_mode.
- Overlapping concurrent work packages edit shared files. — mitigation: Strict per-file ownership. Interfaces (names and signatures) are fixed in this design.
